evidence: Cic. Att. 9.11.1: etsī vix vērī simile est (see “probably”)
terms.comment: Clitipho’s answer in Terence when Syrus’s explanation fits the facts. The same words mean “it is likely” (see “probably”); as a reply to an explanation they say that it makes sense.

terms.gloss: now it makes sense, now I see
evidence: Ter. Haut. 253: Vah, nunc dēmum intellegō.

terms.gloss: that doesn’t make sense, it isn’t plausible
evidence: Ter. And. 225: mīquidem hercle nōn fit vērī simile

terms.gloss: that makes no sense, you’re talking nonsense
evidence: Ter. Eun. 221: Abī, nīl dīcis, Parmenō.

phrases.latin: Fessus est, quia nōn dormīvit. — Vērī simile est.
phrases.english: He’s tired because he hasn’t slept. — That makes sense.

phrases.latin: nunc fīlia postquamst inventa vēra, inventast causa quī tē expellerent. — Est vērī simile.
phrases.english: now that their real daughter has been found, they’ve found a reason to push you out. — That makes sense.

phrases.latin: Vidēn' tū? ancillās, aurum, vestem, quam ego cum ūnā ancillulā hīc relīquī, unde esse cēnsēs? — Vah, nunc dēmum intellegō.
phrases.english: Don’t you see? Maids, gold, clothes, when I left her here with one little maid: where do you think they come from? — Ah, now it makes sense.
Go on, that makes no sense, Parmeno.

sources: Lewis & Short: verus · Lewis & Short: similis · Lewis & Short: intellego
